articles.headline: Notice (Burlington Quarterly Meeting)
articles.author: T. Gould

articles.headline: Obituary (Barbara Sayres)
articles.author: S. S. D.
articles.summary: Died. Barbara, the youngest daughter of Mary and the late Benjamin Sayres, departed this life on the 5th of June, 1865, aged 13 years, 10 months, and 9 days. She was an intelligent child and beloved by all. (Verses follow, signed S. S. D. No place is stated.)
people: deceased, died June 5, 1865 (printed as Barbara, daughter of Mary and the late Benjamin Sayres)

articles.headline: Letter from Salem, N. J.
articles.author: N. H. Turpin
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: I promised to keep you posted in reference to the interesting occurrences of this city. It is a very pleasant place, situated near Fort Delaware, on the Delaware Bay. The colored people in this locality are very industrious; a large number of them are in possession of very comfortable homes. We have one day school, numbering sixty scholars; the teacher is Miss Sheppard. On the 18th, as a number of ladies and gentlemen were returning home from church, they were accosted by a number of rowdies, viz: Irishmen, which resulted in the emptying of the contents of a revolver in the body of one of those [rowdies]. (Dated Salem, N. J., June 30th, 1865; threats to mob the colored people and burn the churches on the night of the 24th followed, and extra police were put on; first quarterly meeting on the 25th; sudden death of Mr. William Hill.)
people: of Salem, N.J.; died suddenly after a fall from a second-story window (as reported)

articles.headline: The 24th U. S. C. T.
articles.summary: We have before us a letter from a non-commissioned officer of the 24th regiment, U. S. C. T., stationed at Point Lookout, Maryland, and present some items therefrom, for the benefit of those who may have friends in the regiment. This fine body of men has been doing guard duty over some 20,000 rebel prisoners at the above named point, where it is likely they will remain until all the prisoners are released. At the request of Mr. John W. Page, we have sent them fifty copies [of the Recorder].
people: 24th U.S.C.T.; at his request fifty copies of the Recorder were sent to the regiment

articles.headline: Florida Correspondence (Third Regt. U.S.C. Troops)
articles.author: Wm. B. Johnson
articles.summary: Headquarters, Post of Jacksonville, June 22, 1865. articles.headline: A Rare Opportunity
articles.summary: A rare opportunity is now afforded to parents who desire to obtain for their children a good trade. We have been applied to by a gentleman of worth, residing in the country, to secure for him an apprentice or two to the boot-making business; would prefer to receive applications for boys of 14 or 15 years.

articles.headline: In Memoriam (Charlotte Bass)
articles.author: J. H. K.
articles.summary: Vincennes, Ind., June 26th, 1865. Charlotte, wife of Rev. L. W. Bass, of the African M. E. Church, Vincennes, Indiana, died in the parsonage of said Church, June 26th, in the 54th year of her age. The deceased was born near Baltimore, and in early life was taken to the city of Philadelphia, where she remained until she reached her womanhood. Here, when quite young, she united with the African M. E. Church, and embraced religion.
people: deceased, died June 26, 1865 at Vincennes, Ind., in her 54th year; raised in Philadelphia, where she joined the African M. E. Church (printed 'Charlotte, wife of Rev. L. W. Bass')

articles.headline: The Late Dr. J. H. Wilson
articles.author: B.
articles.summary: Dr. James Henry Wilson died at 5 1/2 o'clock on Sunday Morning, 9th inst., of acute dysentery, after a short but painful illness of two weeks, in the 47th year of his age. Dr. Wilson was the eldest son of James Wilson, whose manly form and stern virtues our oldest citizens well recollect. He was carefully reared and educated under the direction of strong-minded, pious parents; went through the schools then accessible to young colored men in our city, and is remembered by those who knew him in his school-days, as a bright lad, generally at the head of his class.
people: deceased physician, died July 9, 1865 in his 47th year (Dr.; headline 'Dr. J. H. Wilson'); physician to the Home for Aged Colored Women; vestryman of St. Thomas'; of the drug store of Wilson and Peck, Lombard Street below Seventh
father of the deceased; remembered with his wife as a leading member of Bethel A.M.E. Church

articles.summary: Rev. W. D. W. Schureman will (D. V.) preach at Bethel church on Sabbath afternoon, 16th inst., at 3 o'clock, at which time a collection will be taken up in aid of his church, now in course of erection at Baltimore.
people: to preach at Bethel church, July 16 (Rev.)

articles.headline: Indisposed
articles.summary: The Editor of this paper was so indisposed that he was unable to read the proof-sheets of last week's paper, which accounts for the blunder in our reply to Dr. Thompson, of the 'Advocate and Journal.' We were made to say that in our opinion there was no need for the existence of our Church as an independent body, while we wrote just the reverse. We are still unable to attend to editorial duties, but thought to be improving.

articles.headline: Dr. H. S. Phillips
articles.summary: We refer our readers to the advertisement of the above-named physician, which will be found among our notices. He claims to treat disease by a method not usually practised, and which may be very remedial. He can be consulted at 823 Race Street. His terms to those in needy circumstances are very low, and, in some cases, gratuitous.
people: practical magnetic physician, 823 Race Street (Dr.; not known to be Black)

articles.headline: The Demise of Dr. J. H. Wilson
articles.author: Sea Side
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: The loss of useful and talented men is at all times a great public calamity, but in the lamented death of such a man as Dr. Wilson, the stroke falls on us with crushing weight and tenfold severity. Dr. Wilson was well skilled in his noble department of science, and eminently successful in practice in the city of Philadelphia. (The writer adds that 'we have none other in the regular medical practice'.)

articles.headline: Notice to the Afflicted (Dr. H. S. Phillips; Madam Julien)
articles.summary: Dr. H. S. Phillips, Practical Magnetic Physician for Chronic Diseases, has taken rooms at No. 823 Race Street, Philadelphia. By this treatment, chronic diseases are cured in a few minutes. The services of Madam Julien, a remarkable (and only public colored) Clairvoyant and Trance Medium, have been secured, who will give diagnosis and prescriptions for diseases in the abnormal condition. Madam Julien is the grand-daughter of Knickerbocker, a Chief of a tribe of Kanaka Indians, and niece of Lewis Hamilton, the great Portuguese warrior. She was born on the Isle of St. Kitts. (Marked July 15-4t.)
people: practical magnetic physician, No. 823 Race Street (Dr.; not known to be Black)

articles.headline: Obituary (Julia A. Winder)
articles.author: J. Woodlyn
articles.summary: Died, on the 4th of July, 1865, near Bridgeton, N. J., Julia A. Winder, wife of Philip Winder, in the 30th year of her age. She was a very zealous and active member of the A. M. E. Church, at Greenwich, N. J., for over fourteen years, and improved every opportunity to the utmost extent of her abilities.
people: deceased, died July 4, 1865 near Bridgeton, N.J., in her 30th year; member of the A.M.E. Church at Greenwich, N.J.

articles.headline: Obituary. Dr. James H. Wilson (resolutions of the Ladies' Union Association)
articles.author: Amelia E. Mills
articles.summary: At a meeting of the Ladies' Union Association, held Monday evening, 10th inst., the following resolutions were adopted. Whereas, The Almighty has seen fit, in His unsearchable wisdom, to call from our midst by death Dr. James H. Wilson; therefore, Resolved, That we as an association have cause to mourn deeply his loss, as one of our most faithful friends, who, in the midst of opposition, did all in his power to advance the interests of the Association, and who was instrumental in gaining for us aid and friends, where otherwise all might have been a failure.
people: deceased; friend of the Ladies' Union Association (Dr.)

articles.headline: The Right of Suffrage. Important Meeting.
articles.summary: A public meeting, under the auspices of the Social, Civil, and Statistical Association of the Colored people of Pennsylvania, was held in Sansom Street Hall, on Monday evening, 17th inst. The meeting was organized by the appointment of the following officers: President, I. C. Weare. (A list of Vice Presidents and Secretaries follows.) The President, Mr. Isaiah C. Weare, stated that the object of the meeting was to take measures for advocating the right of the colored people of this State, and of the whole country, to the elective franchise.

articles.headline: The Philadelphia "Press" a Weather-cock
articles.summary: During the latter part of President Lincoln's term, the Press of this city steadily pursued a course which gained for it the good will of the colored citizens of Philadelphia. Since the assassination of our noble President, a most wondrous transformation has been wrought. In its leading editorial of Tuesday, the 18th instant, headed 'The Effect of Negro Suffrage on the South,' it distinctly avows itself to be no friend to the colored people.

articles.headline: Rev. John W. Stevenson
articles.summary: This able minister delivered a lecture on last Tuesday evening, in the Union Baptist church on 'Man, considered mentally, morally and physically.' The subject was handled in a manner at once worthy and becoming. On Thursday evening, 20th inst., Rev. S. delivered his able lecture on 'Courtship and Marriage,' which was by many pronounced a most thoughtful discourse. Brother Stevenson is a young man, laboring to obtain an education.
people: lecturer at the Union Baptist church (Rev.)

articles.headline: An Acknowledgment (8th U.S.C.T. collection for Wilberforce University)
articles.author: Wm. P. Woodlin
articles.summary: Near Petersburg, Va., April 28, 1865. Rev. James A. Shorter. Dear Sir: The appeal of the Trustees of the Wilberforce University for aid, in the columns of the Recorder, suggested the idea to a friend of our race, of the following collection; and I, as the agent, am happy to state, that the men of the regiment, representing at least ten different States, have responded to my solicitations with alacrity, and I am enabled to present you, as the result of my labors, the sum of $211. (Signed Wm. P. Woodlin, Musician 8th U.S.C.T., 2d brig., 2d div., 25th Army Corps. A list of about fifty subscribers of the 8th U.S.C.T., dated Chapin's Farm, Va., March 24, 1865, follows; the money was collected on the march after General Lee from Petersburg to Appomattox Court-house.)

articles.headline: Beaufort Correspondence
articles.author: T. G. Steward
articles.summary: Beaufort, S. C., July 10th, 1865. As is known by many of the members of our beloved Church who live in the Philadelphia Conference limits, I was one of the favored few drafted by Bishop Payne to go to South Carolina. (He is appointed to the Beaufort River Circuit and writes: 'Much is being done for the elevation and instruction of our people here, through the unequalled industry and untiring perseverance of Miss Mary Still, and other female teachers from the North. articles.headline: Editorial Correspondence (Cape Island, N. J.)
articles.summary: Cape Island, N. J., July 25, 1865. We arrived here on last Saturday, the 22d, and stopped at the Banneker House, kept by Mr. and Mrs. Teagle. (The editor reports the killing of an Irishman by a colored hotel waiter whom he had struck, and a threatened mob; the guests at the Banneker House, among them, from Philadelphia, Mr. T. J. Dorsey, Mr. Prosser, Mr. Page, Mr. Ross and a number of others; services on Sabbath the 23d with Brother Cornish, the Elder in charge; 'The Island is well represented with Bethel members. It looks as if one third of the members were here'; and Mrs. Hawkins, 'a highly respectable lady of Philadelphia', keeping a fine store for visitors.)
people: guest at the Banneker House, Cape Island, from Philadelphia (Mr.)

articles.headline: Cape Island Correspondence. No. II.
articles.author: Sea Side
articles.summary: Cape Island, July 24th, 1865. The prospects for a grand season never have been more flattering than at the present time. Every conveyance brings large additions to the present numbers. The hotels and boarding-houses are getting completely crowded with fashionable guests. (Sections: Incidents; Pleasure; A Fatal Affray; Religious; New Comers. The Rev. J. Cornish is on the island to see what he can do towards paying the debts of the Church; the Banneker House 'is the only place for colored guests here'.)

articles.headline: Our Health
articles.summary: We wish to say again, to our very numerous friends, that we have reason to thank Almighty God, that through His kind mercy, and the physician, we are again restored to health. By visiting Cape Island the pure salt air braced us up wonderfully, indeed.

articles.headline: Our Western Tour
articles.summary: We shall, Providence permitting, preach in Cleveland, Ohio, in Rev. John A. Warren's charge, on the 1st Sunday in August, and during our stay there, we expect to visit Oberlin College. The second Sabbath in August, we expect to be in Chicago, with Rev. A. T. Hall. We shall leave there for the Missouri Conference, which meets in Springfield.

articles.headline: Music in the South
articles.author: A. Burris
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: Since my last letter appeared in the Recorder, circumstances have thrown me far into the sunny regions of the South. (Dated Natchez, Miss., July 15th, 1865. He recalls 'the many happy moments I have spent in commingling my voice and emotions with the Sabbath school children of my native city', describes a concert by colored performers at the New Orleans Opera House on June 12th that 'would be very likely to make our Philadelphia ladies look about themselves', and his presiding at the piano on June 28th for Prof. P. H. Murray at St. James chapel.)

articles.headline: Letter from Texas (41st U. S. C. Troops)
articles.author: M. R. Williams
articles.summary: Brazos, Santiago, Texas, June 30th, 1865. Mr. Editor: I take this opportunity of communicating through the columns of your valuable paper, concerning the treatment of the U. S. C. Troops stationed here. I do not think that the government is aware of our situation. Before being detailed to this post, being of the 25th Army Corps, we composed a part of the Army of the James. (Signed M. R. Williams, Co. E, 41st U. S. C. Troops: half rations, pay once in nine months, the poorest medical attendance, one cup of water per day; 'There is laying here now, in the same condition, the 41st, 8th, 127th, and 45th Regt's, all from Pennsylvania'; 'our average loss is three men per day, for the want of food and water'.)

articles.summary: Letter dated Charleston, S.C., July 22, 1865, on the work of the A.M.E. mission in South Carolina. In passing it reports that 'Rev. Jonathan C. Gibbs, of Philadelphia,' is on his way to Charleston to look after the Presbyterian Church of that place.
people: of Philadelphia, on his way to Charleston for the Presbyterian Church (Rev.)

articles.headline: Letter from Charleston
articles.author: E. J. Adams
articles.summary: Letter dated Charleston, July 26, 1865. 'Rev. Mr. Cain, late of Brooklyn, and Rev. J. C. Gibbs of Philadelphia, arrived here a week ago.' Mr. Gibbs has entered upon his duties at Zion Church, sent down as agent for the General Assembly (O. S.).
people: of Philadelphia; at Zion Church, Charleston, agent of the General Assembly, O. S. (Rev.)

articles.headline: Editorial Correspondence. Our Visit to Cape Island [Concluded]
articles.summary: Dated Cape Island, July 26. The editor (Elisha Weaver) describes the colored visitors at the Cape. On Wednesday morning James Rodgers of Baltimore had a girl, Maria Cornette of Frederick, Md., brought to the United States Hotel and jailed on a charge of stealing a diamond ring worth $100; 'Rev. Stephen Smith ... at once proceeded to the Mayor and entered bail,' and she was taken to the Banneker House.

articles.headline: The Christian Recorder: An Appeal to our Ministers, Members and Friends
articles.summary: Standing appeal of the Book Steward offering the paper to January 1, 1866 for $1.75 (tagged July 1, 8t). Repeats weekly.

articles.headline: Notice (Pauline Medora Green)
articles.summary: 'Pauline Medora Green will hear something to her advantage by calling at No. 613, Barclay street, Philadelphia, Pa.'
people: sought; to call at No. 613 Barclay street, Philadelphia

articles.headline: Notice (harvest home, Buckingham Mountain)
articles.author: Jacob Jay
articles.summary: 'There will be a harvest home held on Buckingham Mountain, five miles from Lambertville Station, on the Belvidere Railroad, ten miles from Attleborough, Pa., on Thursday, August 10th, 1865. Tickets to be had on the ground. Dinner served for fifty cents.' Signed Jacob Jay, minister in charge.

articles.headline: Notice (Ladies' Union Association officers)
articles.summary: 'At a stated meeting of the Ladies' Union Association, the following named persons were elected officers for the ensuing year,' followed by five officers.
people: secretary, Ladies' Union Association (Miss); signs the acknowledgment as S. Lizzie Brown

articles.author: S. Lizzie Brown
articles.summary: 'The Ladies' Union Association acknowledge with much pleasure, the following donations from Newport, through the efforts of Mrs. M. Haines: From Bethel Mount Zion Church, $7.57 [VERIFY]; Shiloh Baptist, $19; from Friends, $3.12, and one box of fancy articles.' Signed S. Lizzie Brown, Sec'y.

articles.headline: Notice (Apple Dumpling Festival, A.M.E. Wesley Church)
articles.summary: 'A committee of ladies will give a grand Apple Dumpling Festival, in the basement of the A. M. E. Wesley Church, in Hurst Street, between Fifth and Sixth, and below Lombard street, on Thursday, August 12, 1865, for the benefit of the Church.' Admission 15 cents; tickets at 619 Pine Street. Tagged August 5, 2t.
people: committee, Apple Dumpling Festival, Wesley Church
committee, Apple Dumpling Festival, Wesley Church

articles.headline: Notice (Bishop Wayman's appointments for August)
articles.author: A. W. Wayman
articles.summary: 'Bishop Wayman's appointments for August: Thursday night, 10th, Harrisburg, Pa. Friday night, 11th, Williamsport, Pa. Sabbath, 13th, Buffalo, New York. From thence, God willing, we will travel to the Indiana Conference, at Springfield, Illinois.' Signed W.

articles.headline: Information Wanted (Abbie Davis)
articles.author: Rachel Davis
articles.summary: 'Of Abbie Davis, daughter of Rachel Davis, who was born at Wilmington, Delaware. She was carried to Cuba ... over thirty-five years ago.' Later in Texas and New Orleans, where she kept a wash house about 1862. Replies to Rachel Davis, care Christian Recorder, Box 2975, Philadelphia. Tagged Aug. 5, 2t.

articles.headline: Excursion (Macedonia Sabbath School, Camden)
articles.summary: 'The annual excursion of the Macedonia Sabbath School, of Camden, N. J., to Red Bank, will take place on Thursday, August 17, 1865. The steamer Eagle will leave Kaighn's Point at 7 1/2 o'clock, A. M., touching at Philadelphia. Tickets, Adults 40 cents; children half price. They may be had at this office.'
people: committee of arrangements, Macedonia Sabbath School excursion, Camden
committee of arrangements, Macedonia Sabbath School excursion, Camden

articles.headline: Married
articles.summary: Two marriages at Newport, R.I., July 20, 1865, by Rev. E. T. Williams: Charles Barton to Miss Emily J. Anderson, at the residence of James Palmer; and at the residence of the bride, Mr. Sampson Fay of Jones County, N.C., to Mrs. Harriet Hill of Philadelphia, Pa. [names read on the two-column crop only; VERIFY]

articles.headline: Coal Yard. Thos. J. Bowers
articles.summary: 'Coal Yard. Thos. J. Bowers, (At 634 Lombard Street, above Sixth, Phila.,) has constantly on hand the best Lehigh, Schuylkill and other Coal, at the Lowest Market Price. Coal and Kindling Wood always on hand by small measure.' Orders also received at a number on South Second Street (number not legible). A new, larger ad; the older 'Coal! Coal!!' card of T. J. Bowers (634 Lombard) still runs on page 3.
people: proprietor, coal yard, 634 Lombard Street above Sixth

articles.headline: From Petersburg, Va. (library and Bible from the Shiloh Baptist Sabbath School of Philadelphia)
articles.author: Anna R. Robinson
articles.summary: 'The Library and a handsome Bible were purchased by a society of young ladies attached to the Sabbath School of Shiloh Baptist Church of Philadelphia. The President of the Society, and the Treasurer, brought the articles to this city accompanied by the following address,' dated Philadelphia, July 14th, 1865, to the Gilfield Baptist Church, Petersburg, Va. Signed Anna R. Robinson and Fannie J. Robinson, Petersburg, Va., July 20th, 1865.
people: treasurer, young ladies' society of the Shiloh Baptist Sabbath School; co-signer

articles.headline: Emancipation Celebration at Bath, Penna.
articles.summary: 'A meeting of the colored citizens of Bethlehem was held at Bath, Pa., on the 1st inst., to celebrate the West Indian Emancipation. The following gentlemen were appointed officers for the day: President, Enoch Emory; Vice-President, H. B. Black; Secretary, Wm. N. Stout.' Addresses by Lewis Nicholson, H. B. Black, James H. Wilson and 'the Rev. James H. Smith, of Philadelphia.'
people: of Philadelphia; delivered an address at the Bath celebration (Rev.)

articles.headline: Letter from Bro. Seaton
articles.author: D. P. Seaton
articles.summary: Letter from Wilmington, Del., July 29, on the session there of the M. E. Colored Mission Conference and the visit of an A.M.E. Zion delegation; the two bodies agreed to meet in convention in Philadelphia in November.

articles.headline: Letter from the 3d U.S.C.T.
articles.author: Wm. B. Johnson
articles.summary: Letter from Jacksonville, Fla., July 27, 1865, by the Post Clerk, Co. A, on the condition of the Third U.S. Colored Troops (raised at Camp William Penn) and its commander, Brevet Brig. Gen. B. C. Tilghman. No Philadelphia men are named in the part read.

articles.headline: Editorial Correspondence. Sketches by the Wayside
articles.summary: The editor left Philadelphia on Wednesday, August 2, 1865, for the Western conferences, stopping at Pittsburgh (Rev. Samuel Watts; Rev. Lewis Woodson of Allen Chapel) and Cleveland (Rev. John A. Warren).

articles.headline: The City
articles.summary: 'A larger number than usual of our prominent citizens are absent this season from the city; some rusticating among embowered groves, reclining carelessly beside beautiful streams.' Others are at the sea shore. No names given.

articles.headline: Delaware Colored Mission Annual Conference of the M. E. Church
articles.author: Frisby J. Cooper
articles.summary: Journal of a trip through Delaware (July 22-26) and of the conference at Wilmington, Bishop Scott presiding, Bishop A. W. Wayman present. Delegates from the A.M.E. Zion Church (S. T. Jones, Bro. Boslee, S. Golden) visited 'to confer with them on the union of the two bodies'; they decided to hold a convention 'some time in November, 1865, at Zoar Church, Philadelphia.' Appointments, Delaware River District: J. G. Manluff, P. E.; John Wesley Station, A. Brown; Zoar, to be supplied; Camden, J. H. Pearce.

articles.headline: Convention of Colored Men of New Jersey
articles.author: Wm. Steward
articles.summary: 'According to a call issued by the Equal Right's League, of Trenton, N. J., the people of New Jersey (colored) sent delegates, who met in Convention at Trenton, on the 13th of July, (1865,) which, after becoming organized, formed an association styled "The Equal Right's League of New Jersey."' Officers follow. Signed Wm. Steward, Rec. Sec'y.
people: vice president, Equal Rights League of New Jersey; of Burlington (Rev.)

articles.headline: Notice (Apple Dumpling Festival, A.M.E. Wesley Church; date changed)
articles.summary: Same notice as August 5, but the date now reads 'on Monday, August 14, 1865.' Committee printed clearly here: Elizabeth Smith, Amelia J. Spriggs, Ann Hollingsworth. Admission 15 cents; tickets at 619 Pine Street.
people: committee, Apple Dumpling Festival, Wesley Church
committee, Apple Dumpling Festival, Wesley Church
committee, Apple Dumpling Festival, Wesley Church

articles.headline: $25 Reward (John Hunt and Pauline Green)
articles.summary: 'Twenty-five dollars is offered for the arrest of John Hunt or Pauline Green, or both. The latter left her home, at Orange, N. J., with and through the persuasion of the said John Hunt, on the 7th of July last.' She is between 16 and 17; both are colored. Address a woman at Orange, N.J. (name not legible). Compare the Pauline Medora Green notice of August 5 (613 Barclay street, Philadelphia).

articles.headline: Information Wanted (Robinson children, of Fauquier County, Va.)
articles.summary: 'Of Loudon Beckwith, Joseph, and Maria Jane Robinson, children of Samson and Jane Robinson, who came from Fauquier County, Va., about ten years ago.' Information to their sister Eliza Ellen, at Attleborough, Bucks Co., Pa. (surname not legible). Tagged Aug. 12, 3t.

articles.headline: Obituary. Rev. Jeremiah Asher
articles.author: J. H. P.
articles.summary: Dated Head Quarters 27th U.S.C.T., Wilmington, North Carolina, July 30th, 1865. 'Rev. Jeremiah Asher, Chaplain of the 6th U.S.C.T., was attacked by a bilious disease a few weeks ago. ... He died on the 27th of July, 1865.' He 'leaves a dear wife and family'; Mr. and Mrs. Day took him into their own house during his illness, and 'Mr. Day has accompanied the body home to the afflicted wife and friends.'
people: deceased, July 27, 1865, at Wilmington, N.C.; chaplain of the 6th U.S.C.T. (Rev.)

articles.headline: 25th U.S.C.T.
articles.summary: 'We have before us a letter from Sergeant D. H. Williams, Co. K, 25th Regt. U.S.C.T., in which he states that a rumor is in circulation to the effect, that his regiment is about to be discharged. We merely mention this item, as many of the members of said regiment have friends in Philadelphia and vicinity.'
people: sergeant, Co. K, 25th U.S.C.T.; letter writer

articles.headline: Rev. James Lynch
articles.summary: 'We are pleased to say to our readers and brother Lynch's personal friends that he arrived in this city on Wednesday. Any despatches for him may be sent to our care until further notice.'
people: A.M.E. missionary from Georgia; arrived in Philadelphia Wednesday, August 16 (Rev.)

articles.headline: National Equal Rights' League
articles.summary: Editorial notice that the National Equal Rights League will assemble at Cleveland, Ohio, on the first Tuesday in September, by call of its President, John M. Langston; see the Special Notice dated from the League's Bureau at Philadelphia.

articles.headline: Letter from Cape Island
articles.author: Sea-Side
articles.summary: Letter resumed August 15, 1865. The season closed with a masquerade ball at Congress Hall on the 8th. 'Mrs. Teagle, the Proprietress of the Banneker House, has been fortunate this season in having a very liberal patronage'; the house is said to be for sale, with talk of a stock company of colored men buying it. Rev. John Cornish is working to pay the $600 debt on the Visitor's A. Meth. E. Church.
people: pastor, Visitors' A.M.E. Church, Cape Island (Rev.)
preached at Cape Island, Sunday evening, August 13 (Rev.)

articles.headline: A Cheering Word
articles.author: Wm. Nesbit
articles.summary: 'Mr. Editor: The Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League, which has just closed its annual meeting at Harrisburg, Pa., having passed a resolution that its members should seek to make the Christian Recorder their medium of communication, I take the earliest opportunity to say that I hope you will devote one corner of your excellent journal to the use and benefit of the objects and operations of the League.' Dated Altoona, August 14, 1865.

articles.headline: Special Notice. Bureau of National Equal Rights League, Philada., August 14, 1865
articles.author: St. George R. Taylor
articles.summary: 'Gentlemen and Members of National Equal Rights League: You and the representatives from the organizations within your respective States, are requested to attend the first annual session of the League on the first Tuesday of September, 1865, at 10 o'clock A. M., in Cleveland, O.' By order of the President of the N. E. R. League, John M. Langston. St. George R. Taylor, Secretary. Tagged Aug. 19, 3t (ends on page 3).
people: Secretary, National Equal Rights League (Bureau at Philadelphia)

articles.headline: Resolutions Passed (Young Men's Christian Association, Shiloh Baptist Sabbath School)
articles.author: John H. Carter
articles.summary: 'At a stated meeting of the Young Men's Christian Association attached to the Shiloh Baptist Sabbath School, held August 8th, 1865, the following preamble and resolutions were unanimously adopted: Whereas, it has pleased Almighty God ... to take from our midst at this critical time our much beloved pastor and brother, Rev. Jeremiah Asher, whilst performing his duties on the battle field.' Signed John H. Carter, President; Robert H. Cooper, Sec'y.
people: secretary, Young Men's Christian Association of the Shiloh Baptist Sabbath School

Bethlehem Church, Pearl street, Burlington, will hold a Harvest Home for the benefit of their Church, in the City Park, on Thursday, August 24th, 1865, at which time addresses will be delivered by Revs. J. articles.summary: 'There will be a celebration of several benevolent societies given at Langhorn's Hill, near Attleborough, Bucks county, Pa., September 7th, 1865. Reached by the Market street Ferry and West Jersey Rail Road, or the South St. Ferry to Gloucester and stage. Signed by the Elder in Charge (name not legible) and a committee of three.

The boat will leave Jersey Ferry, Camden, N. J., at quarter after 7 o'clock, and South Street Ferry, Phila., at 8 o'clock.' Returns at 5 P.M., stopping at Old Chester. Tickets $1.00. articles.headline: Married
articles.summary: 'On the 15th inst., by Rev. Jacob Mitchell, Mr. William S. Walker, Sr., of Millersville, Lancaster County, Pa., to Miss Elizabeth R. Wicks, of New York. articles.headline: Ladies' Fair at Beaufort, S. C.
articles.summary: Letter dated Beaufort, S.C., Aug. 14th, 1865. 'On the evening of August 2d, a few ladies met at the "Lincoln House," to consider the propriety of holding a fair, to aid the destitute Freedmen on Edisto Island, and other places in South Carolina.' On August 7, at the A.M.E. Bethel Church, 'The Ladies' Fair, of Beaufort' was formed: Mrs. Sarah Bram, President; Miss Mary Still, Vice President; Mrs. Robert Small, Treasurer; Miss Jennie Lynch, Secretary.

articles.headline: Letter from Bethlehem
articles.author: Enoch Emory
articles.summary: Dated Bethlehem, Penna., August 14th, 1865. Bethlehem has about one hundred and fifty colored persons 'without churches or sabbath schools'; God 'has sent us a man from your city, by the name of Rev. James H. Smith, who has established a church and also a sabbath school with fifteen scholars and two teachers.' He preached first in a private house, then in a hall holding five to six hundred persons.
people: 'a man from your city' (Philadelphia); established a church and Sabbath school at Bethlehem (Rev.)

articles.headline: Proceedings of the Annual Meeting of the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League, held in the City of Harrisburg, August 9th and 10th, 1865
articles.summary: Editor's note: 'We have received from Mr. J. C. White, Jr., the worthy Rec. Sec. of the P. E. R. League, a copy of the proceedings of the State Convention, held in Harrisburg, Aug. 9th and 10th,' the remainder to follow in later issues. The League met in the Union Wesleyan Church, Harrisburg, on Wednesday morning, August 9, at 10 o'clock, and was called to order by the President, Mr. Peck, who read the 27th Psalm; prayer by Rev. J. Henry. Thirty-one members answered the roll.
people: of Philadelphia; chairman, Committee on Credentials; the League's Solicitor

articles.headline: The City
articles.summary: Local column: citizens are returning from the country and the sea shore. No Philadelphians are named.

articles.headline: Presentation to Elder Moore
articles.summary: 'The Missionary Society of Bethel A. M. E. Church will present to Rev. Wm. Moore and wife suitable tokens of regard, on Monday evening, 28th inst., at 8 o'clock, at Sansom street Hall. The presentation speech will be made by Mr. I. C. Wears, who, with other gentlemen, will make brief addresses on the occasion. Proceeds for the benefit of the Home for Aged Colored persons.'
people: recipient, with his wife, of tokens from the Missionary Society of Bethel (Rev.)

articles.author: H. J. Rhodes
articles.summary: Account of a collecting tour for an A.M.E. Zion mission church: he left Philadelphia on July 6, visited Woodbury, N.J., and other places, and returned to Philadelphia. Read for names on the two-column crop only; no Philadelphia persons are named in the part read.

articles.headline: Rev. Jeremiah Asher (funeral; from the National Baptist)
articles.summary: Reprinted from the National Baptist of the 17th. Rev. Jeremiah Asher died at Wilmington, N.C., July 27; the body was brought to the city and the funeral was held at Shiloh church on Tuesday afternoon, the 8th inst. The ministers assembled at his late residence in Rodman street and walked in procession to the church. He was ordained at Providence about 25 years ago, was pastor of Shiloh for 14 years and chaplain of the 6th regiment about two years; aged 52.

people: 'of Philadelphia'; address at the Charleston celebration (Rev.)

articles.author: Richard Barney
articles.summary: 'My Quarterly Conferences will take place the 9th of September, at Frogtown; on the 16th and 17th, at Bushtown; 23d and 24th at Woodbury, and on the 30th, at Small Gloucester.' Signed Richard Barney, Minister.

articles.headline: Notice (Grand Union Emancipation Meeting, Penningtonville)
articles.summary: 'The colored people of Penningtonville, Penna., will celebrate the 1st of September by a Grand Union Emancipation Meeting, in Sherlott's [VERIFY] Woods, one quarter of a mile from Penningtonville. Central Railroad, 'beginning on August 30th. During that time the Masons and Samaritans will parade, and have sermons delivered to them, and the Sabbath School will hold its harvest home.' Asbury church of the same circuit holds its harvest home August 26th.

articles.headline: Bethel Sabbath School

articles.headline: Enterprise among our Colored Men
articles.summary: We take great pleasure in noticing the fact, that our men of color are beginning to realize the fact that more men of business are needed among them. Several have already shown that they understand this. We will not now particularize, but shall do so in an early number.

articles.headline: A Correction
articles.summary: In our last issue, in the marriage by Rev. J. H. Lowber [VERIFY initials], the lady's name should have been inserted Mrs. Eliza Hazzard, of New London, Penn. Bro. Lowber threw us completely off the track, and caused us to neglect congratulating the happy couple, which we now do.

articles.headline: The Excursion to Atlantic City
articles.summary: In another column will be found an advertisement of an excursion from our friends to Atlantic city. It promises to be one of the most recherche of the season. The price of tickets is $1.25, which answers going and returning. From the names of those having the matter in charge, we anticipate it will be a success. Mr. Bryant, the well known manager of the road, will spare no pains to provide for the comfort of all who may desire to attend.

articles.headline: Bethel A. M. E. Sabbath School
articles.summary: This, the oldest, and probably the largest and best Sabbath school belonging to the A. M. E. Church in America, celebrated last Wednesday, 30th inst., by an excursion to Diamond Cottage. The morning was everything else except a favorable one, but as old Sol began to shine forth and the lowering clouds to disperse, the hearts of thousands were made glad, in anticipation of a merry time.

articles.headline: For the Sea Shore. A Grand Excursion and Pic-nic to Atlantic City (For Colored Persons Exclusively)
articles.summary: Will take place on Tuesday, Sept. 5, 1865. Fare going and returning, $1.25. Children under 10 years of age, 65 cts. Tickets for sale at the Railroad Office, at the wharf, two hours before starting. Last Boat leaves Vine St. Ferry at 6.30 A. M. Committee of Arrangements.

M. By order of the R. W. G. Chief.

articles.headline: Notice (Brick Wesley Sabbath School excursion)
articles.summary: The Brick Wesley Sabbath School will make its Annual Excursion on Thursday, September 14th.

articles.headline: Banneker House, Cape Island, New Jersey (Mrs. Teagle); Mrs. H. C. Lunn's Boarding House, Cape Island
articles.summary: Mrs. Teagle of the Banneker House, Cape Island, New Jersey, would respectfully present this Circular for your favorable consideration, and informs her friends and the public, that she will re-open her house on the 20th day of June, for the reception of persons who may desire to resort to this beautiful watering place. articles.headline: Home for Disabled Colored Soldiers. An Appeal
articles.author: Anne de B. Mears
articles.summary: We take peculiar pleasure in calling attention to the letter published below, which has been sent us by a lady well known to many of our brave soldiers, who have experienced the benefits of her kind consideration while in the hospital at Camp William Penn. To the Editor of the Christian Recorder: Sir: Through the columns of your widely-circulated paper among the colored population of Philadelphia and elsewhere, I wish to make an appeal in behalf of the disabled colored soldiers who have been discharged from the service, many of them have no homes or any one to care for them.

articles.headline: Wanted (workmen on tin and sheet-iron)
articles.author: Wm. Still
articles.summary: The subscriber is in want of several good workmen on tin and sheet-iron in his stove store. Freedmen or others deprived of following their trades, owing to the controlling prejudices of white mechanics, would do well to apply immediately, as the highest wages will be paid. Besides this, to such as may prove capable and steady, a rare chance is offered for advancement in a business aspect. Wm. Still, Stove Warehouse, 107 North Fifth Street, Philadelphia. (Sept. 9, 3t.)

articles.headline: Letter from Texas (29th Connecticut Volunteers)
articles.author: Charles W. Cole
articles.summary: 29th Reg't. Conn. Vols., Brownsville, Texas, August, 20th, 1865. Mr. Editor: Sir, I have for a long time been a steady peruser of your valuable paper, and have found much therein to cultivate a good mind. It was sent to me by a friend in Philadelphia, during most of the time that I spent in Virginia, in the campaign of 1864. As there are few in our ranks from Philadelphia and none of them seem inclined to do so, I take the liberty to pen you a few lines.

articles.headline: Delays are Dangerous

articles.headline: Shameful
articles.summary: A few days ago, a very distinguished lady of our acquaintance, and another from Baltimore, got into one of the Spruce and Pine Street cars. Upon collecting the fare, the conductor discovered that they were colored persons. They were ordered to quit the car, but declined doing so. The car was then driven off at a furious rate.

articles.headline: The Institute for Colored Youth
articles.summary: Miss Grace A. Mapps, who has for some twelve years been one of the teachers in this school, has resigned her charge as Principal of the Girls' department. Miss Mapps has been a faithful laborer in the cause of education. Miss Fanny Jackson, one of Oberlin's best graduates, has taken Miss Mapp's place. We know of no one who is better fitted to fill the vacancy in every way than Miss Fanny Jackson, in a moral, religious, and literary capacity.

articles.headline: Stove Store
articles.summary: Our old and well known business friend, Mr. Wm. Still, of this city, has entered quite extensively into the stove and coal business. We hope our Philadelphia friends will patronize him in his line of trade. Our friend, Mr. Bowers, is also carrying on the same business in Lombard St. for the benefit of our people and all others who may favor him with a call.

articles.headline: Missionary Prayer Meeting (Bethel church)
articles.summary: Bethel church has organized a missionary prayer-meeting. This is right, and it is one of the best steps the church has ever taken. We hope that on next Tuesday night the basement of the church will be crowded to its utmost capacity, as at this time we purpose to complete its organization.

articles.headline: Quarterly Meeting; Home Again; Papers from Barbadoes
articles.summary: The Mission church, of which Rev. H. J. Rhodes is pastor, will hold its quarterly meeting next Sabbath, as also does the Macedonia church, Camden, New Jersey, of which Rev. G. A. Boyer is pastor. Home Again: Once more, by the blessing of God, notwithstanding old Satan's attempt, we have reached our home in safety. Papers from Barbadoes: Our thanks are due to our worthy friend and brother, Mr. Joseph Atwell, (who is from Barbadoes, and studying here in the Episcopal Theological Seminary, to better prepare himself for the ministry,) for the presentation of several late Barbadoes papers.
people: pastor, Macedonia church, Camden, New Jersey (Rev.)

articles.headline: Stove Store (William Still, 107 North Fifth Street)

Ranges: The National Range, Philadelphia Range, Globe Range, &c. Heaters: The Vulcan, &c. Casting for repairs. Job work promptly attended to. William Still, 107 North Fifth Street, Philadelphia. Orders received for Lehigh and Schuylkill Coal.

articles.headline: Return of Thanks. To the pastor, members, and congregation of Union M. E. Church, 4th St., below Arch
articles.author: Jno. W. Stevenson
articles.summary: My Dear Friends: I take this method of returning to you my most heartfelt thanks for your most generous donation of $186 on Sabbath, the 10th inst. To myself it was like the dews of heaven, striving, as I am, at the same time, to bring sinners into the fold, and cultivate what intellect God has been pleased to bestow upon me. Your gift shall be held in grateful remembrance so long as life lasts.

articles.headline: Notices (Frankford Circuit quarterly meetings; Salem, N. J.)
articles.author: J. H. Smith

people: elder in charge, Salem city, N. J.

articles.headline: An Acknowledgment (Ladies' Union Association)

articles.headline: Funeral Sermon (Wesley church, Hurst street)
articles.author: J. Mitchell
articles.summary: The Rev. Elisha Weaver, Editor of the Christian Recorder, will preach a funeral discourse in Wesley church, Hurst street, on next Sabbath, at 10 1/2 o'clock. The friends are requested to turn out early on the occasion. J. Mitchell, Pastor.

articles.headline: Notice (farewell sermon of Rev. James Hamilton, Union Baptist Church)
articles.summary: The Rev. James Hamilton will, God willing, deliver his farewell sermon, at the Union Baptist Church, Minster street, on Sabbath evening, the 24th inst. Rev. Hamilton has been appointed to the charge of the African Baptist Church, in Charleston, South Carolina, and will enter upon his duties as soon as possible. people: Baptist minister leaving for Charleston, S. C. (Rev.)

articles.author: E. C. Cooper
articles.summary: Died, in Chatham, C. W., on the 23d of August, 1865, Sister Matilda Jackson, formerly Mrs. Matilda Kelly, aged 45 years. Mrs. Jackson was a member of the A. M. E. Church in Philadelphia, Pa. She was known to be one of the most active members of her church while there. She came to Chatham in 1850, when the cholera was raging. He was the son of the late Rev. Daniel H. and Mary Peterson. Aged 28 years. Due notice will be given of the funeral.

articles.headline: "A Hop at the Banneker House" (reply)
articles.author: Ann M. Teagle
articles.summary: As there has been an article published in the columns of the Recorder, we will admit a reply, which shall end the entire affair in our paper. Ed. Mr. Editor: In your edition of the 2d inst., appeared an article with the above caption, and, as the sentiments therein contained do not agree with the facts, I have taken the liberty to address you. During the past season I kept the Banneker House at Cape Island, N. J., and endeavored in every way to make it comfortable and pleasant for my numerous boarders.

articles.headline: Prejudice
articles.author: Johnson Woodlin
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: As it is said that the rebellion is passing away, and that slavery is following in the same train, we also desire that every incident which this doubled-dyed system of iniquity has engendered shall likewise be numbered with the things that were. We ask that prejudice against a man, or set of men, because he or they be not of the same color as another man, or set of men, shall also be obliterated. (Dated Philada., Sep. 23d, 1865; argues for the franchise for the freedmen.)

articles.headline: From Salem, N. J.

articles.headline: Great Odd Fellow's Celebration at Baltimore, Md., on the 6th of October
articles.summary: This bids fair to be the grandest affair ever given in this country by colored people. The members have also made arrangements with the Baltimore Railroad Company, so that ladies and gentlemen can make the round trip for $4.50. They can extend their stay, if they wish, to ten days.

events.name: Death of Dr. James Henry Wilson, physician
events.location: Philadelphia
events.description: Dr. James Henry Wilson died at 5 1/2 o'clock on Sunday morning, July 9, 1865, of acute dysentery after two weeks' illness, in the 47th year of his age. Memoir signed 'B.': eldest son of James Wilson; educated in the schools then open to young colored men in the city; barred by caste from the medical schools, he hired himself at the Academy of Natural Sciences, then in the College of Pharmacy, then at Jefferson Medical College and afterwards the Medical Department of the University of Pennsylvania, completing the curriculum of each by private study; he applied for a degree and after long equivocation the examining board answered that it was inexpedient to examine any colored candidate. Leading physicians nevertheless admitted him to consultation. Lately appointed physician to the 'Home for Aged Colored Women' (so printed). He kept a drug store in partnership with Dr. Peck, son of the Rev. John Peck of Pittsburg (Wilson and Peck, Lombard Street below Seventh), then entered practice. His parents are remembered as leading members of Bethel A.M.E. Church; he was for many years a member of St. Thomas' (Episcopal) church and often an active vestryman. 'A man of unmixed African blood, short in stature'; 'probably more widely known and beloved by the colored people of Philadelphia than any man now living'. Twice married; leaves a wife, a daughter and two sons (the youngest two years old) and one brother, the last of a family of seven. On page 3 a letter signed 'Sea Side' laments that 'we have none other in the regular medical practice', and the Ladies' Union Association prints resolutions.

events.location: Philadelphia (place not stated)

Signed Amelia E. Mills, President; S. Lizzie Brown, Secretary.

events.name: Social, Civil, and Statistical Association of the Colored People of Pennsylvania: public meeting on the right of suffrage
events.location: Sansom Street Hall, Philadelphia
events.description: Public meeting under the auspices of the Social, Civil, and Statistical Association of the Colored people of Pennsylvania, Monday evening, July 17, 1865. Officers appointed: President, I. C. Weare (Mr. Isaiah C. Weare). Vice Presidents: U. B. Vidal, Stephen Smith, Clayton Miller, James P. Clay, Wm. Whipper, Morris Brown [VERIFY], Henry Jones, Robert Adger, Jos. M. Bustill [VERIFY], T. H. Davis, Rev. Wm. Moore, C. Simpson, Rev. E. Weaver, H. Morton, Daniel George, Wm. H. Riley, Henry Gordon, J. W. Price, S. H. Herrott [VERIFY], J. Hankinson, Wm. S. Burton [VERIFY], J. E. Glasgow, J. M. Autor [VERIFY], Joshua Brown, C. H. Bustill, B. G. Hill [VERIFY], R. Jones, S. Purnell, M. R. Robinson. Secretaries: Wm. Still, S. Morgan Smith, Raymond J. Barr [VERIFY], P. T. Smith, C. J. Houston [VERIFY], R. M. Adger, A. S. Casey [VERIFY], J. C. White, Jr., St. George Taylor, H. Johnson, R. Faucet, Thomas H. Boling. The President said the object was to take measures for advocating the right of the colored people of this State and of the whole country to the elective franchise; friends say 'You are right, but do not hold any meetings; it will all come right'; the present action of the Government tended to hand the colored man over to those who oppressed him before the war. Rev. W. J. Alston was announced as first speaker but declined from indisposition. Rev. C. W. Denison spoke (he came 'to hear colored men speak in behalf of their own rights, after speaking so well with the bayonet'), then Rev. Dr. Wood, a native of England; Messrs. Robt. Purvis and S. Morgan Smith also spoke. The Chairman offered resolutions, which were adopted: to spare no pains in pressing the claim to suffrage; to circulate Wm. D. Kelley's speech on the 'Safeguards of Personal Liberty', Fred. Douglass' address on 'Equality before the Law' and R. Dale Owen's letter to President Johnson; that the colored citizens of Philadelphia give liberally to vindicate their rights through newspapers, pamphlets and public meetings. S. Morgan Smith offered a further resolution, adopted, extending to the Convention to be assembled at Harrisburg the Association's cordial co-operation. Announced as the first of a series of meetings; well attended, 'the audience being composed of both classes'.
attendees: Secretary; spoke and offered a resolution of co-operation with the Harrisburg Convention

events.name: Cape Island, N.J.: the editor's visit, the Banneker House and the fatal affray of July 23
events.location: Cape Island (Cape May), New Jersey
events.description: Two accounts in this issue. The editor (Editorial Correspondence, dated July 25) arrived Saturday July 22 and stopped at the Banneker House, kept by Mr. and Mrs. Teagle; guests there included Mrs. Jordon and son and Bro. Burly and lady, of Baltimore, and from Philadelphia Mr. T. J. Dorsey, Mr. Prosser, Mr. Page, Mr. Ross and others. On Sabbath the 23d he attended the colored church with Mrs. Jordon and Rev. Turpin; Brother Cornish, the Elder in charge, was trying to raise $50; two sisters sat in the pulpit, one of them Sister Murray, a preaching woman. 'The Island is well represented with Bethel members. It looks as if one third of the members were here.' Mrs. Hawkins, 'a highly respectable lady of Philadelphia', keeps a fine store for visitors and does more business than any other store of the kind there (the editor points to her advertisement in the Recorder); Brother and Sister Fields keep a grocery store. Both the editor and the correspondent 'Sea Side' (July 24) report that on that Sabbath a white man (an Irishman, the editor says) struck a colored man employed at a hotel or billiard saloon; the colored man struck back, a brick was thrown and the white man died; two colored men were held, the Irish threatened to mob the colored people and the Mayor advised them to desist. Sea Side adds that the Banneker House is the only place for colored guests on the island.
attendees: guest at the Banneker House, from Philadelphia (Mr.)

events.location: Cape Island, N.J. (United States Hotel; Banneker House; A.M.E. Church)

Wayman at night.

events.name: First of August (West India Emancipation) celebration at Bath, Pa.
events.location: Bath, Northampton County, Pa.
events.description: The colored citizens of Bethlehem met at Bath on August 1, 1865, to celebrate West Indian Emancipation (the 31st anniversary). Officers of the day: President, Enoch Emory; Vice-President, H. B. Black; Secretary, Wm. N. Stout. Lewis Nicholson made the introductory remarks; H. B. Black and James H. Wilson spoke (Wilson on the promotion of colored soldiers and Pennsylvania's duty to give the colored man his rights); 'the Rev. James H. Smith, of Philadelphia,' delivered an address. events.name: Equal Rights League of New Jersey -- formed in convention at Trenton

The city was full of returning soldiers waiting for their pay, but all passed off quietly. Officers for the ensuing year: President, Samuel G. Gould, of Trenton; Vice Presidents, Rev. events.name: M. E. Colored Mission Conference and A.M.E. Zion delegates -- union convention appointed for Zoar Church, Philadelphia

Golden) conferred on the union of the two bodies. Elsey, Harrison Smith and John G. Manluff. Appointments, Delaware River District: J. G. Manluff, presiding elder; John Wesley Station, A. Brown; Zoar, to be supplied; Camden, J. H. Pearce; Salem, N. Young. Reported by Frisby J. Cooper. None linked (M. E. clergy of the Delaware conference).

events.name: Apple Dumpling Festival, A.M.E. Wesley Church (Hurst Street)
events.location: Basement of the A.M.E. Wesley Church, Hurst Street between Fifth and Sixth, below Lombard, Philadelphia

events.name: Death of Rev. Jeremiah Asher, chaplain of the 6th U.S.C.T.
events.location: Wilmington, N.C.
events.description: Rev. Jeremiah Asher, chaplain of the 6th U.S. Colored Troops (and pastor of Shiloh Baptist Church, Philadelphia, though the obituary does not say so), died of a bilious disease at Wilmington, N.C., on July 27, 1865, after some weeks' illness in the house of Mr. and Mrs. Day. events.name: Cape Island: Banneker House season and benefits for the Visitors' A.M.E. Church
events.location: Cape Island, N.J.
events.description: 'Sea-Side' reports (August 15) that Mrs. Teagle of the Banneker House had a very liberal patronage; the house is rumored for sale to a stock company of colored men. Rev. John Cornish has $200 in hand toward the $600 debt of the Visitors' A.M.E. Church. A concert for the church was given on the 9th (the writer criticizes the pronunciation); Rev. William Moore preached on Sunday evening the 13th and raised nearly $200 [VERIFY amount]; a son of Rev. Wm. H. Jones gave a Magic Lantern exhibition on Monday the 14th, yielding $25.

events.name: Young Men's Christian Association, Shiloh Baptist Sabbath School -- stated meeting; resolutions on the death of Rev. Jeremiah Asher
events.location: Shiloh Baptist Church, Philadelphia
events.description: At a stated meeting on August 8, 1865, the Young Men's Christian Association attached to the Shiloh Baptist Sabbath School unanimously adopted a preamble and resolutions on the death of 'our much beloved pastor and brother, Rev. Jeremiah Asher, whilst performing his duties on the battle field': the Association has lost a dear friend, the Church a faithful pastor, and the army a dutiful chaplain; sympathy to the bereaved family; the Association to go in mourning for six months; the resolutions to be published in the Christian Recorder. events.location: A.M.E. Wesley Church, Hurst Street, Philadelphia
events.description: The official board met and, on the motion of the Steward, unanimously adopted five resolutions: there is a growing interest among the membership and religion is reviving through Rev. Jacob Mitchell; the Bishop's appointment is 'the right man in the right place'; in the past twelve years there has never been such a quarterly meeting; Mitchell is a God-fearing minister and a good governor; the board, 'his cabinet,' bind themselves to assist him. Signed (as read at high resolution): John H. Hughes, Gassaway Chase [VERIFY], Geo. Hollingsworth, Sherry Kennard [VERIFY], Luke Quann [VERIFY], Caleb Bell, Robert Boyer, Joseph C. Miller [VERIFY: C. or G.], Perry M. Chambers, William Waters, Mitchell Lewis, Daniel Harris, Emory Johnson, Charles Dingle, Noah Fisher, Burton Harman [VERIFY], David Cole, Wesley James. Mitchell's residence is No. 513 Lombard Street, east of 5th; he may be found in his study in the church from nine to twelve daily. In the evening a grand concert in the church by the Sabbath School, conducted by Mr. Joseph Freeman, 'the celebrated chorister of Philadelphia'; doors open at 7, admittance 20 cents, children under 12 half price. Theodore Gould, Pastor.
attendees: conductor of the concert; chorister, of Philadelphia

events.name: Celebration of several benevolent societies at Langhorn's Hill, near Attleborough
events.location: Langhorn's Hill, near Attleborough, Bucks County, Pa.
events.description: Several benevolent societies (not named) will hold a celebration at Langhorn's Hill near Attleborough on September 7, 1865, and invite 'all like institutions and a generous public.' Dinner on the ground at 50 cents; feed for horses furnished. By order of the committee: Thomas Growden [VERIFY], Pres.; John Newman, Sec.

events.name: Union Camp Meeting, Carpenter's Landing, Gloucester County, N.J.
events.location: Grounds of Mr. West Jessup, Carpenter's Landing, Gloucester County, N.J.
events.description: Union Camp Meeting to commence August 25, 1865; no money paid or promised for the ground. Pastors and people are invited to erect private tents; boarding tents are limited. Reached by the Market street Ferry and West Jersey Rail Road to Carpenter's Landing (one mile to the camp) or the South St. Ferry to Gloucester and 8 miles by stage. Signed by the Elder in Charge, whose name reads 'J. P. Hamer' or 'Bamer' [VERIFY]. Committee: Edward Kirkman, 914 Rodman St., near 10th, Phila.; George Washington, 522 South 5th Street, Phila.; James Tudas, Woodbury, N.J.

events.name: Union Methodist Church Quarterly Meeting at Wilmington -- steamboat excursion from Camden and Philadelphia
events.location: Wilmington, Del.; steamboat Eagle from Jersey Ferry, Camden, and South Street Ferry, Philadelphia
events.description: Quarterly Meeting of the Union Methodist Church at Wilmington, Delaware, Sunday, August 27, 1865. The steamboat Eagle is chartered: leaves Jersey Ferry, Camden, at 7:15 and South Street Ferry, Philadelphia, at 8 o'clock; leaves Wilmington for Philadelphia at 5 P.M., stopping at Old Chester both ways. Refreshments on board; tickets $1.00. No names are given.

events.name: Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League: annual meeting at Harrisburg
events.location: Union Wesleyan Church, Harrisburg, Pa.
events.description: First instalment of the official proceedings, furnished by the Recording Secretary, J. C. White, Jr. The League met on Wednesday, August 9, 1865, at 10 A.M. President Peck called the meeting to order and read the 27th Psalm; prayer by Rev. J. Henry; the President gave an address; 31 members answered the roll. On motion of Mr. Bustill of Philadelphia, T. Morris Chester and William H. Parham, Esqs., reporters of the 'Press' and the 'Colored Citizen,' were invited to seats. Committee on Credentials: J. C. Bustill of Philadelphia, chairman; Dan'l Williams of Hollidaysburg; Aaron L. Still of Reading; E. R. Parker of Allegheny; Chas. H. Kelley of Williamsport. Henry B. Fry of Reading was made Assistant Secretary pro tem. Committee of three on rules: Dr. J. McC. Crummill of Philadelphia, chairman; Nathaniel W. Depee of Philadelphia; O. L. C. Hughes of Harrisburg. A debate on who might sit as members followed (Bustill; Nesbit of Altoona; Williams of Hollidaysburg; Prof. Vashon of Pittsburg; J. C. White, Jr., of Philadelphia, who distinguished three classes of members; Hughes and Vance of Harrisburg; Still of Reading). 'Mr. Solicitor Bustill paid forty dollars ($40) from the following auxiliary Leagues': No. 10, Rising Sun E. R. League, 2d district of Philadelphia; No. 11, New Castle, Lawrence Co.; No. 12, Benevolent, Erie; No. 13, Bellefonte, Centre Co. Bustill's resolution that no association be represented unless its fee was paid was carried. Adjourned to 2 1/2 o'clock. The officers' election and the delegate roll are not in this instalment (to be continued in later issues). || From the Christian Recorder of August 19, page 2: Wm. Nesbit, writing from Altoona on August 14, 1865, reports that the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League 'has just closed its annual meeting at Harrisburg' and passed a resolution that its members make the Christian Recorder their medium of communication; he asks the editor for a corner of the paper for the League, and urges the forming of auxiliary leagues. No delegates or officers are named in this issue. In the same issue the Bureau of the National Equal Rights League, dated Philadelphia, August 14, 1865, calls the first annual session at Cleveland, Ohio, for the first Tuesday of September (September 5), 1865, at 10 A.M., by order of President John M. Langston; St. George R. Taylor, Secretary. || From the Christian Recorder of September 2, page 1: Continuation of the proceedings (the first part ran the week before). Afternoon session, 2 1/2 o'clock, President Peck in the chair. Rules of order reported by the Committee on Rules (James McC. Crummill of Philadelphia, chairman; O. L. C. Hughes; Nath'l. W. Depee): three sessions daily, the evening one public; one-third of enrolled members a quorum; Matthias's Manual to govern. Solicitor Bustill paid in forty dollars from auxiliaries No. 14, Altoona E. R. League ($15, representatives Wm. Nesbit and John Alexander), No. 15, Hollidaysburg E. R. League ($15, Dan'l. Williams and Moses Brown) and No. 16, Huntingdon E. R. League ($10, John G. Chaplin). Committee on Credentials (Joseph C. Bustill, chairman; Daniel Williams; Aaron L. Still; E. R. Parker; C. H. Kelley [VERIFY]) certified these representatives: Henderson Davis, Jr., Lincoln E. R. League, 1st District of Philadelphia; Lorenzo D. Blackston [VERIFY], Rising Sun E. R. League, 2d District of Philadelphia; Chas. W. Nighten [VERIFY], New Castle E. R. League, Lawrence Co.; Henry T. Burley, Benevolent E. R. League, Erie; Franklin Johnson, Bellefonte E. R. League, Centre Co.; William Nesbit and John Alexander, Altoona; Daniel Williams and Moses Brown, Hollidaysburg; John G. Chaplin, Huntingdon. Henry T. Burley of Erie made Assistant Secretary pro tem. On motion of J. C. White, Jr., of Philadelphia, a Business Committee was named: Prof. G. B. Vashon of Pittsburg, chairman; O. L. C. Hughes of Harrisburg; B. Pulpress of Allegheny City; William D. Forten of Philadelphia; Rev. James Henry of Birmingham; later enlarged, on motion of Mr. Bustill, by Jas. McC. Crummill of Philadelphia, C. W. Nighten of New Castle, John Alexander of Altoona and Aaron L. Still of Reading. Finance Committee: Nath'l. W. Depee of Philadelphia, chairman; Edward R. Parker of Allegheny City; Samuel Molson [VERIFY] of Lewistown; George W. Dimey of Allegheny City; Rev. C. J. Carter of Harrisburg. Mr. Bustill of Philadelphia offered resolutions on the circulation of petitions and invited the choirs of the city to furnish music at the evening meetings; Mr. Fauset [VERIFY] of Philadelphia offered a resolution on the collection of statistics, and later one on the taxation of auxiliary leagues by membership. The Business Committee's report urged leagues in every county, town, village and hamlet, spoke of colored people 'taunted, insulted and cowardly assaulted on the highways by ruffians, on rail-roads by conductors, and driven from hotels and places of amusement', and offered a petition to Congress for a constitutional amendment forbidding legislation against any civilized portion of the inhabitants on account of race or color, with resolutions to petition the Pennsylvania Legislature, to send blank petitions to every League, Church and Lodge, and to appoint canvassers to gather statistics of the numbers, wealth and occupation of the colored people of the State. Finance Committee (N. W. Depee) recommended a one dollar tax; at the evening session (8 o'clock, President Peck in the chair) this was amended on motion of J. C. White, Jr., to tax every member of the League one dollar. Article 10th of the State League constitution was struck out and Article 12th amended, on Mr. Bustill's motions, to let auxiliaries connect directly with the National Equal Rights' League. An amendment by Prof. G. B. Vashon giving extra votes for cash paid in was voted down. Solicitor Bustill reported No. 17, Pittsburg E. R. League (Prof. Geo. B. Vashon, representative), with its ten dollar fee. The choirs of the city sang 'My Country, 'tis of thee'. The meeting went into committee of the whole on the state of the League, Mr. J. C. Bustill of Philadelphia in the chair, and adjourned to 10 o'clock the next morning.

of Philadelphia; Recording Secretary (printed 'J. C. White, Jr.')
secretary, National Equal Rights League; notice dated from its Bureau at Philadelphia
chairman, Committee on Rules; added to the Business Committee; of Philadelphia (Dr.)
Committee on Rules; chairman, Finance Committee; of Philadelphia
